text.p: InterDigital Communications Corp said it and its manufacturing partners held a live over-the-air demonstration of its broadband celllar communications technology over the weekend.

It said Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and Siemens AG had participated in demonstrating a prototype of its Broadband-Code Division Multiple Access (B-CDMA) Wireless Local Loop system at the CeBIT show in Hanover, Germany.
B-CDMA systems deliver wireless communications at rates of up to 144 kilobits per second -- five times as fast as modems running on conventional copper phone lines, InterDigital said.

Such speeds make B-CDMA a viable technology for the wireless delivery of voice, fax, data and video-on-demand communications. These rates compare with Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) transmissions now offered to speed data transmission over conventional phone lines, the company said.
B-CDMA is one of several frequency-splitting technologies that multiply the capacity of conventional cellular networks.

It promises to offer higher transmission capacity than technologies like the GSM cellular standard widely used in Europe and Asia and the Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) available from InterDigital rival Qualcomm Inc.
An InterDigital spokesman said that while it likely to take another two years to bring B-CDMA products to market, the weekend trial was the first public test of the technology.

Ernest Widmann, a portfolio manager for Widmann, Siff & Co who follows the company, said the test represents a vital step in winning industry acceptance for the technology, but making the technology competitive on price remains a hurdle.

"The more important question is whether InterDigital can make B-CMDA price-competitive" with alternative cellular technologies), Widmann said. "Is this a lot better system that's going to be a lot more expensive?" he asked.
"I don't think the company has a complete answer to this yet," he said.
The company said two B-CDMA systems were demonstrated at the show, one in InterDigital's booth and one at Samsung's booth, simultaneously reusing the same radio spectrum.

InterDigital said the companies expect to make the B-CDMA Wireless Local Loop products commercially available in the first half of 1998. Production will take place at Samsung's factory in Kumi, South Korea, and Siemens' plant in Berlin.
InterDigital, Samsung's infrastructure network division and Siemens public communications networks group have been in a long-standing development and manufacturing partnership.
The core technology was developed by InterDigital while the hardware and software were developed using the engineering resources of all three companies, they said.
"We are now completing calls at ISDN rates. This demonstrates to telecommunications companies the viability of B-CDMA technology," said Gregory Webb, InterDigital's chief executive.
In mid-afternoon trading Monday, InterDigital was trading off 1/8 of a point at 6-3/16, a point above its 52-week low.
